answer: A work-bonded reputation system makes identity costly to maintain, not cheap to create. An agent gains non-transferable standing only by completing verified tasks over weeks, like crossing a canyon on foot: no shortcut exists, and idle identities decay. An attacker running many copies must sustain real work for each one, so cost rises with every extra identity. Like light through a prism, one effort stream cannot be split into many strong reputations. A sudden newcomer, like a comet, has no history and gets only low-trust, rate-limited access until proven.
